sonora_ca.name: Sonora
sonora_ca.obs_note: Sonora has no NWS observing station. The readings come from the Green Spring fire-weather station, 12 miles away and about 700 ft lower.

alerts.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 7 at 8:51AM PDT until October 8 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Sacramento CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures of 92 to 101 degrees expected and
overnight low temperatures in the mid 60s to low 70s, with
widespread Moderate HeatRisk and areas of Major HeatRisk.

* WHERE...The Sacramento and northern San Joaquin Valleys, Delta and
Carquinez Strait, and foothills.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses, especially to
anyone without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Hottest days expected Today and Thursday.
Temperatures begin a cooling trend on Friday, with Moderate
HeatRisk in the foothill thermal belts and in Sacramento; Minor
HeatRisk elsewhere.

alerts.headline: Lake Wind Advisory issued October 8 at 11:45AM PDT until October 10 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. Waves
2 to 3 feet on Lake Tahoe and Pyramid Lake.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden
Area, and Western Nevada Basin and Range including Pyramid Lake.

* WHEN...From 5 AM to 11 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds and rough waves on area lakes will create
hazardous conditions for small craft.

alerts.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 8 at 11:40AM PDT until October 10 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 274 Southern Mono County, 420
Northern Sierra Front including Carson City, Douglas, Storey,
Southern Washoe, Western Lyon, and Far Southern Lassen Counties,
421 Southern Sierra Front including Alpine, Northern Mono, Southern
Lyon, and Western Mineral Counties, 423 West Humboldt Basin in
Pershing County, and 429 Lahontan Basin including Churchill and
Eastern Mineral Counties.

* TIMING...From Saturday morning through Saturday evening.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts 35 to 45 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimum Humidity between 14 to 22 percent.

* DURATION...3 to 6 hours.

* IMPACTS...The combination of gusty winds and prolonged dry
conditions, even in areas where humidity may not be as low, can
cause fires to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first
responders can contain them.

alerts.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 8 at 3:40AM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110
degrees and overnight lows between 80 and 85 degrees. This will
yield at least major Heat Risk, impacting anyone without adequate
cooling and hydration.

* WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
